reference: GNU nohup supplies the functional parity oracle. Help and version identify bash-os and are checked as documented metadata contracts; GNU branding and release numbers are not functional compatibility requirements. Child commands use private fixtures only.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata contract
Argument boundaries and exported environment passed to a child
Relative fixture file creation, directory creation, and removal through child commands
Missing command and operand/option error boundaries
TTY-specific descriptor redirection and terminal hangup behavior recorded as deferred
exclusions: TTY stdin/stdout/stderr combinations, nohup.out append behavior, and HOME fallback need a disposable PTY fixture; the supplied runner uses stdin /dev/null and captured pipes.
Survival across a controlling-terminal hangup needs a disposable PTY session with a controlled terminal disconnect. No signal operation is run in this suite.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash identifies nohup as a builtin and provides a nonempty help topic, independently of GNU nohup output.
A private child expands the exported variable itself and prints exact empty, spaced, wildcard and shell-looking literal argv.
cases.script:
export NOHUP_PARITY_VALUE='exported value'
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' 'printf "env=<%s>\n" "$NOHUP_PARITY_VALUE"' 'printf "arg=<%s>\n" "$@"' > child
chmod 755 child
nohup ./child '' 'two words' '*' '$(touch injected)'

cases.purpose: Verify nohup returns the child's nonzero exit status while leaving stdout and stderr empty.
cases.script:
rc=0
nohup false || rc=$?
printf 'child-status=%s\n' "$rc"
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Run the ordinary touch operation through nohup on a relative path inside the private fixture tree; compare the resulting file and mode with GNU.
Run mkdir through nohup on a relative fixture path and compare the created directory and permissions with GNU.
Remove a small relative fixture file through nohup and compare the final file tree with GNU.
cases.script:
printf 'private fixture\n' > fixture-file
nohup rm fixture-file
printf 'removed\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented 127 status when command lookup fails, without relying on any installed command or credential.
Check GNU's missing-operand status and its treatment of an unrecognized leading-dash command name; print both statuses so a candidate mismatch remains visible.
cases.script:
missing=0
nohup || missing=$?
leading_dash=0
nohup --bash-os-nohup-command-that-does-not-exist || leading_dash=$?
printf 'missing=%s leading-dash=%s\n' "$missing" "$leading_dash"

cases.purpose: The loadable help describes its command and signal behavior.
cases.script: metadata=$(nohup --help); [[ $metadata == *'Run CMD with SIGHUP ignored'* && $metadata == *'CMD may be an enabled shell builtin or an external executable.'* ]]; printf 'help-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Version output identifies the loadable implementation without claiming to be the GNU release.
The tty branches select /dev/null for terminal stdin and append terminal stdout to nohup.out, with related stderr routing and HOME fallback.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable PTY fixture that can assign stdin/stdout/stderr as tty or pipe independently, inspect nohup.out contents and mode, and arrange a relative nohup.out open failure to exercise the HOME fallback. The supplied runner uses stdin /dev/null plus captured output pipes, so it cannot establish these conditions.

cases.purpose: Verify the child ignores SIGHUP across a controlled controlling-terminal disconnect.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable PTY session and a helper that closes the PTY master to generate hangup only for the fixture's foreground process group, then observes the child's completion and status. This runner has no PTY control interface; no process signal is sent by this suite.

cases.purpose: A relative nonexecutable regular file produces GNU status 126.
cases.script:
printf bytes > child
chmod 600 child
nohup ./child
